From the owner
Drafty doors and windows in Michigan homes, and why they show up every fall - The first cold morning of October tells you a lot about your house. You notice the chill by the front door, the curtain that moves on its own and the bedroom that never quite warms up. Drafty doors and windows are the most common comfort complaint we hear from Southeast Michigan homeowners, and most of them can be fixed with carpentry rather than a replacement quote. Our draft sealing service exists because the fix is usually smaller than people fear. This guide walks through every place cold air gets past a door or a window, what you can check yourself on a Saturday and what calls for a trained set of hands. It covers entry doors, storm doors, patio doors, double-hung sashes, sills, trim and the caulk lines that hold it all together. When a section points to a job our Wright’s Repairs division handles, we link to it so you can see exactly what the visit includes. We are a design-build firm based in Ypsilanti, and over the years our crews have worked in older plaster-wall homes in Ann Arbor, postwar ranches in Westland and newer colonials in Canton. The draft problems look different in each, but the causes repeat. Worn seals, doors that moved out of square, sills that rotted from the bottom and caulk that gave up years ago account for nearly everything we find on a winterizing visit for Michigan homes. How Michigan housing stock shapes the problem...
